info.title: wayhouse controller API

get.description: The CA asks a site's own name on port 80, which a gateway terminates; the gateway forwards that path to any controller node, and this route answers from the replicated store while the order that published it is running. There is no authentication on purpose: the key authorization is what the CA is meant to read, and the token is 128 bits of the CA's choosing that nobody can guess before the order starts. An unknown or expired token is a plain `404`.

parameters.description: The challenge token the CA chose.
parameters.name: token

404.description: No such token, or it is not valid now.

500.description: The store could not be read.

get.description: The CA directory in use and, once the controller has registered, the account URL and the id of the key that seals the account key. Before the first order `account_url` is `null`.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.

get.description: Authenticated with a gateway token (`Authorization: Bearer gwt_...`, from `POST /acme/gateways`) instead of the admin token: the admin token does not work here. Lists the sites that name this gateway and already have a certificate, with the version and expiry. Limited per source address (5 a second, burst 20).

401.description: No token, a malformed one, or an unknown gateway.

429.description: Too many requests from this address. `Retry-After: 1`.

get.summary: List the certificates a gateway may fetch

get.description: Authenticated with a gateway token, as `GET /acme/bundles`. Returns the certificate chain and the private key. The answer carries `ETag: "<version>"`; send it back as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged certificate answers `304`. A site this gateway is not listed on looks the same as one that does not exist. The answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`; serve it over TLS.

304.description: The certificate has not changed since `If-None-Match`.

401.description: No token, a malformed one, or an unknown gateway.

404.description: No such bundle for this gateway, or no certificate has been issued yet.

429.description: Too many requests from this address. `Retry-After: 1`.

503.description: This controller cannot open the certificate key (is the cluster secret key loaded?).

get.summary: Fetch a site's certificate and key

get.description: The gateways that may fetch certificate bundles, and the sites each can reach. Never their tokens or hashes.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.

post.description: Makes a gateway (a machine that terminates TLS for sites, such as Caddy) and its bearer token. The token is in this answer only; the store keeps its hash. It authenticates `GET /acme/bundles` and `GET /acme/bundles/{site}`.

400.description: The body is not `{"name": "..."}` or the name is not 1 to 63 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`.

409.description: A gateway with that name exists: delete it first to issue a new token.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.

delete.description: Its token stops working at once on every replica. Each renewal creates a new key, so a key the gateway held is replaced at the next renewal.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.

get.description: Every site the controller keeps a certificate for, with the current certificate's version and expiry and the state of the last renewal attempt. A site is a set of names that share one certificate. A controller that does not run ACME answers `501` on every `/acme` route.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.

delete.description: Stops renewing the site and removes it. The stored certificate goes with it.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.
This controller does not run ACME.

put.description: Declares the names the site's certificate covers and how the controller proves control of them. With the default `dns-01` challenge a DNS plugin install (`dns_plugin`) must exist, be enabled and have approved the `on_acme_dns` trigger; wildcard names need `dns-01`. With `http-01` the CA is answered at `/.well-known/acme-challenge/{token}` by any controller node (see that route). `gateways` names the gateways that may fetch the site's certificate bundle.

parameters.description: The site's name, 1 to 63 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`.
parameters.name: name

400.description: A malformed body, an invalid site (names, challenge, zone, timeout), or a DNS plugin that is missing, disabled or did not approve `on_acme_dns`.

404.description: A named gateway does not exist.

422.description: A wildcard name without the `dns-01` challenge.

501.description: This controller does not run ACME.

post.description: Step 2 of a key rotation, next to `POST /admin/plugins/secrets/rewrap`: the account key and every certificate key are sealed again under the active secret key. It runs on the leader (a follower forwards it) and is refused while a member lacks the active key.

409.description: The controller has no secret key, or a member lacks the active key or runs an older build, or the write was refused.

503.description: There is no leader to forward to.

post.description: Turns an empty standalone controller into a `slave` tier that relays a parent controller's config and intent streams. It seeds from the parent's current config, then keeps following it; from then on it refuses direct config writes (`403`). It only works on a controller with no revision history, and not on an HA controller (start that tier with `--role slave` instead). There is no API call that undoes it.

200.description: Adopted. `seeded_config_revision` is the parent's revision this tier started from, `null` if the parent had none.

409.description: This controller runs HA, is already a slave, or has revision history.

get.description: The Raft membership as this node sees it: its own id, the leader it knows, the voters and the learners with the addresses the replicas reach them on, and the node's own log position. Answered by any member.

post.description: Adds node `id` at `addr` as a learner, waits for it to catch up and promotes it to a voter. The node must answer `/raft/whoami` as `id` with an empty log. A follower relays the request to the leader (this can take up to five minutes while the node catches up). The answer is the new membership, as `GET /admin/ha/members` gives it. A new replica normally joins by enrollment instead (a `controller` code and `POST /enroll/ha-join`), which needs no admin token on the new host.

409.description: The node is already a voter, or another membership change is in progress.

422.description: A bad body or `addr`; the address did not answer as that node id; the node's log is not empty; or the cluster refused the change.

503.description: No leader is elected yet, the leader changed while forwarding, or the address does not answer.

delete.description: Takes the node out of the membership entirely. Removing the leader is allowed: it steps down once the change commits. The last voter cannot be removed.

404.description: That node is not a member.

409.description: Another membership change is in progress.

422.description: It is the last voter, or the cluster refused the change.

503.description: No leader is elected yet or the leader changed while forwarding.

put.description: Points an existing member at a new address, for a replica that moved. The node must answer `/raft/whoami` as `id` at the new address.

404.description: That node is not a member.

409.description: Another membership change is in progress.

422.description: A bad body or `addr`, or the address did not answer as that node id.

503.description: No leader is elected yet, the leader changed while forwarding, or the address does not answer.

post.description: A proxy tells the controller which of its backends are up, so plugins with the `backends` capability see `backend_health` events. `full: true` means the list is the complete view, otherwise it is a change. The leader keeps the board, so a follower forwards. Gated on the `x-wayhouse-protocol` header; at most 512 KiB.

get.description: The newest revision visible to `group` (a revision staged for a canary group is visible only to that group), as raw YAML. The revision number is in the `X-Config-Revision` header. A revision whose secrets were scrubbed after it was replaced is never returned as current.

parameters.description: The caller's canary group. Absent means no group: only promoted revisions are visible.
parameters.name: group

parameters.description:
The newest config `schema_version` the caller parses: the answer is the newest visible
revision that needs no more. Absent means no limit.
parameters.name: max_schema

parameters.description: Scrub the inline secrets from the text (`settings.admin.auth_token`, `settings.gossip.psk`).
parameters.name: redact

404.description: Nothing visible to this group has been submitted yet.

post.description:
The body is a raw YAML config document, the same shape a proxy's config file has. It is parsed and validated exactly as a proxy would on a reload; a document that fails never touches the store, so the previous revision stays current. On success the document becomes a new revision and every subscriber receives it.

`stage=canary&group=<name>` stages the revision for one canary group instead: only instances that report that group see it until you promote it. `base` guards against overwriting an edit you have not seen. A change that could lock the operator out (the admin listener, its token or TLS, gossip) starts a trial automatically: unless the revision is confirmed in time, the controller re-submits the previous one. `confirm_within` sets or disables the window.

A standby controller (slave tier) refuses writes with `403`. In an HA cluster a follower forwards the write to the leader and relays its answer.

parameters.description:
`canary` stages the revision for one group instead of promoting it. Absent promotes it now;
any other value is a `400`.
parameters.name: stage

parameters.description: The canary group, 1 to 128 bytes. Required with `stage=canary`; one group per submission.
parameters.name: group

parameters.description:
The revision your edit started from (`0` = none yet). `409` if the latest revision is
another one, so a save cannot silently overwrite a newer edit.
parameters.name: base

parameters.description:
Seconds to hold the new revision on trial, 10 to 600: unless it is confirmed
(`POST /config/confirm/{revision}`) by then, the controller re-submits the previous
revision. Absent: a 60 second window when the change could lock the operator out (see
`risks` on `GET /config/pending`), none otherwise. `0`: none, whatever the change.
parameters.name: confirm_within

200.description: Accepted. `revision` is the number the document now has.

400.description: An unknown `stage`; `stage=canary` without a `group` of 1 to 128 bytes; `confirm_within` outside 10 to 600 seconds, on a canary revision, or with no previous revision to fall back to.

403.description: This controller is a slave tier and does not accept writes.

409.description: `base` is not the latest revision (the body carries `current`), or a confirm window needs every HA member to run a build that supports it.

422.description: The document does not parse or validate, or its `schema_version` is newer than the oldest live proxy supports.

503.description: The proxy registry cannot be read to check the schema version.

post.description: Ends the trial in favour of the new revision, which stays as it is.

409.description: That revision is not on trial: it was confirmed, reverted or replaced; or an HA member runs a build that cannot decode trials.

get.description: While a revision is on trial (a risky change, or one submitted with `confirm_within`) this reports it with the time left, so every operator's page shows the same countdown. `risks` lists what makes a change risky.

200.description: `pending` is `null` when nothing is on trial.

post.description: Makes a revision staged with `stage=canary` visible to everyone. It is the one change that does not create a revision: it flips the visibility of an existing one. Promoting an already promoted revision is a no-op. It can start a confirm trial like a submission does.

parameters.description:
Seconds to hold the promoted revision on trial, 10 to 600, as on `POST /config`. Absent: a
60 second window when promoting could lock the operator out, none otherwise. `0`: none.
parameters.name: confirm_within

400.description: `confirm_within` is out of range or has no previous revision to fall back to.

403.description: This controller is a slave tier and does not accept writes.

It is the most guarded route: a 1 KiB body limit, at most 10 tries a minute per client address (a /64 for IPv6) and 5 per code id, and one answer (`401`) for every wrong, spent, expired or other-role code. A success is not counted against the limits. Every value in the answer is a secret; the answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`. Serve it over TLS.

A request is counted against a per-source limit (5 a second, burst 20) before the token is compared, then against a per-install limit (10 a second, burst 20); the body is at most 256 KiB. While the `plugin_webhooks` feature flag is off every call answers `503`.
